reference: Bash type/help metadata and the documented custom nc connect/listen/scan parser contract. Safe invalid-argument cases return before address resolution or socket creation. There is no matching GNU CLI; all socket operations remain deferred.
coverage: Bash metadata reports nc as a builtin with no PATH executable resolution.
Bash help exposes the documented nc verbs, options, constraints and deferred features.
Deferred TCP connect transfer and idle timeout behavior.
Deferred explicit-address, one-peer TCP listener behavior.
Deferred UDP request/reply and first-peer response behavior.
Deferred TCP scan open/closed range output and status behavior.
Deferred usage and decimal range validation.
Safe missing-operand/unknown-verb and invalid-wait parser contracts; no socket or DNS activity.
exclusions: No network or authentication operation executes; parser cases lack required peer operands and return before socket/DNS calls.
No matching GNU netcat CLI implements this custom verb API.
TCP/UDP operation coverage requires a future disposable VM with a reviewed socket mock; metadata and parser results are not transfer/listener/scan coverage.
Proxy, TLS, keep-listen and broker/relay modes are outside the documented v1 interface.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash classifies nc as a builtin when candidate execution has an empty PATH.
Confirm Bash reports only the builtin definition and does not resolve an executable through PATH.
Check help output against the documented nc_doc contract, including the verb synopsis, explicit listen address, timeout semantics and v1 limitations.
cases.stdout:
nc: nc
    Netcat-style TCP/UDP scratch tool (subset).
    
        nc connect HOST PORT [-u] [-w SECS]   TCP/UDP client
        nc listen  PORT -s ADDR [-u] [-w SECS]   bind + accept-one (TCP) / recv (UDP)
        nc scan    HOST FIRST [LAST] [-w SECS]   -z TCP port scan
        nc --version
    -w bounds TCP connect/accept, writes and idle reads (timeout returns 1);
    for UDP it sets the reply drain window after stdin EOF. Zero uses defaults.
    
    Multiplexes stdin and the socket via epoll(7). Listen mode requires
    explicit `-s ADDR`; use `-s 127.0.0.1` for loopback or `-s 0.0.0.0`
    to expose externally. v1 always exits after the first connection (no -k);
    SOCKS proxy, TLS, broker mode, and named-pipe wiring are deferred.

cases.purpose: Exercise TCP connect mode's binary stdin-to-peer stream, EOF half-close, peer-to-stdout stream and clean success status.
Exercise the documented finite -w timeout while a connected TCP peer accepts but stays idle, including failure status and shell continuation.
Exercise TCP listen mode's mandatory explicit -s address, one accepted peer, bidirectional streaming and v1 exit after that peer.
Exercise UDP connect mode's request payload and post-stdin-EOF reply drain window.
Exercise UDP listen mode's first-datagram source caching and response of stdin bytes to that peer.
Exercise TCP scan over a small range containing one controlled open and one closed loopback port, plus the documented closed-only result.
Exercise documented usage failures for missing operands, malformed or out-of-range decimal ports, reversed scan ranges and invalid -w values before any socket action.

cases.script:
for verb in connect listen scan unknown; do
 if nc "$verb"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 printf '%s=%s\n' "$verb" "$rc"
 [[ $rc == 2 ]]
done
cases.purpose: Missing required arguments and unknown verbs return before address resolution or socket creation, as verified by source control flow; diagnostics remain visible.

cases.script:
for value in -1 nope 1.5; do
 if nc connect -w "$value"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 printf '%s\n' "$rc"
 [[ $rc == 2 ]]
done
cases.purpose: Invalid wait values reject during argument parsing; no host or port operand is supplied and no network call can follow.
